headline: Binance $6.3B heist, freezer sabotage and AI-driven attacks dominate
overview: The biggest story is the $6.3 billion Binance crypto theft, which reportedly began with a supply-chain compromise and a fake job interview, with North Korea denying involvement. AI is a recurring theme, from an infostealer that uses LLMs to rank victims to attackers running up cloud AI bills with stolen keys. Physical-world and infrastructure threats also featured, including supermarket freezers switched to defrost mode and an actively exploited Siemens Node-RED flaw.

topStories.title: Binance $6.3B crypto heist
topStories.summary: Binance says the October 29 theft started with a June supply-chain compromise and escalated through a fake hiring process that delivered poisoned developer tools. Attackers reached the internal wallet signing service. North Korea denied links as researchers traced the stolen funds.

topStories.title: AI-enabled attacks and LLMjacking
topStories.summary: Talos described the VOLTA infostealer, which uses LLMs to analyse stolen data and prioritise victims by monetisation value. Google and Mandiant flagged LLMjacking, where stolen API keys or cloud tokens run up rapid AI bills, and the UK NCSC warned AI will routinely feature in nation-state attacks.

topStories.title: Supermarket freezer sabotage
topStories.summary: Attackers hit refrigeration controllers at hundreds of European supermarkets, switching freezers into defrost mode. US investigators are treating August commissary freezer failures as suspected cyberattacks, with weak default passwords on exposed controllers reported.

topStories.title: Actively exploited Siemens Node-RED flaw
topStories.summary: VulnCheck observed attackers exploiting a critical missing-authentication flaw in the Node-RED admin interface of Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 devices to deploy bots. Siemens has issued a patch.

topStories.title: Election and government targeting
topStories.summary: CISA is reportedly scaling back its Election Day role, while a US election commission was targeted. Germany said lawmakers' iPhones may have been hacked with spyware, and NCSC and NATO activity added to the government threat picture.

topStories.title: Ransomware and secrets exposure
topStories.summary: Ransomware is encrypting outdated Synology NAS devices, and Trigger.dev customers were told to rotate their secrets after an exposure. Langflow also fixed a critical login bypass and RCE.

episodes.summary: Talos discusses the VOLTA infostealer, which uses LLMs to rank stolen victims by value and reads session data such as email and order histories. Includes defender advice.
